Ἐλιούδ.long: Eliud, son of Achim, and father of Eleazar.
Ἐλιούδ.sd: God of majesty; Eliud, an Israelite
Ἐλιούδ.as:
Ἐλιούδ, ὁ
indecl.,
Eliud, an ancestor of Jesus: Mt 1:14, 15.†

Ἐλεάζαρ.long: Eleazar, son of Eliud, and father of Matthan.

ἐλάχιστος.long: least, smallest, but perhaps oftener in the weaker sense: very little, very small.
ἐλάχιστος.sd: used as equivalent to G3398 (μικρός); least (in size, amount, dignity, etc.)
ἐλάχιστος.as:
ἐλάχιστος, -η, -ον
(v.s. ἐλάσσων),
smallest, least: as proper superlat., I Co 15:9; elsewhere, as usually in late Gk., intensive (B1., § 11, 3); Mt 2:6(LXX)25:40, 45, Lk 12:2616:1019:17, I Co 4:36:2, Ja 3:4; ἐ. ἐν τ. βασιλείᾳ τ. οὐρανῶν, Mt 5:19 (v. Dalman, Words, 113). Compar., ἐλαχιστότερος (for corresp. superl., v. LS; v. also Bl., § 44, 3); less than the least: Eph 3:8.†

ἐλεήμων.as:
ἐλεήμων, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for חַנּוּן ;]
merciful:Mt 5:7, He 2:17.†

ἐλεάω.sd: to compassionate (by word or deed, specially, by divine grace)
ἐλεάω.kj: have compassion (pity on), have (obtain, receive, shew) mercy (on)
ἐλεάω.as:
† ἐλεάω, later form of ἐλεέω, q.v.,
[in LXX as v.l. in To 13:2, Ps 37:26, al. ;]
in NT: Ro 9:16, Ju 23, WH.†

ἐλεημοσύνη.long: abstr: alms-giving, charity; concr: alms, charity.
ἐλεημοσύνη.sd: compassionateness, i.e. (as exercised towards the poor) beneficence, or (concretely) a benefaction
ἐλεημοσύνη.as:
† ἐλεημοσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(< ἐλεέω), [in LXX chiefly for חֶסֶד, צְדָקָה ;]
1.mercy, pity.
2.almsgiving, alms (like the German Almosen, a corruption of the Greek word ἐ): Mt 6:4; ποιεῖν ἐ., Mt 6:2, 3, Ac 9:3610:224:17; ἐ. διδόναι, Lk 11:41 (cf. Mt 23:36; Dalman, Words, 62 f.) 12:33; αἰτεῖν, Ac 3:2; λαβεῖν, Ac 3:3; πρὸς (in order to ask) ἐ., Ac 3:10; pl., Ac 10:4, 31 (Cremer, 711).†

ἔλεος.as:
ἔλεος, -ους, τό
(cl. -ου, ὁ, and so Rec., Mt 9:1312:723:23, Tit 3:5, He 4:16; on the Hellenistic form τό ἔ., v. WH, App., 158; M, Pr., 60; Mayser, 277; Kühner, i, 515), [in LXX chiefly for חֶסֶד ;]
mercy, pity, compassion;
1. of men: Mt 9:13(LXX)Mt 12:723:23; ποιεῖν ἔ. (and id. seq. μετά, c. gen.; cf. Heb.עִםחֶסֶדעָשָׂה, Ge 21:23, al.), Lk 10:37, Ja 2:133:17.
2. Of God: Lk 1:50, 541:58, Ro 15:9, Eph 2:4, II Ti 1:161:18, Tit 3:5, He 4:16, I Pe 1:3; esp. in benedictions, Ga 6:16, I Ti 1:2, II Ti 1:2, II Jo 3, Ju 2; σκευὴ ἐλέους, Ro 9:23; σπλάγχνα ἐλέους, Lk 1:78; ποιεῖν ἔ. (v. supr.), Lk 1:72; τ. ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει, Ro 11:31.
3. Of Christ: Ju 21.†
SYN.: οἰκτιρμός (v.s. ἐλεέω)

ἐλαφρός.der: probably akin to G1643 (ἐλαύνω) and the base of G1640 (ἐλάσσων);
ἐλαφρός.as:
ἐλαφρός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for קַל, קָלָל ;]
light in weight easy to bear: Mt 11:30; θλίψρις (EV, our light affliction), II Co 4:17.†

ἐλπίζω.long: I hope, hope for, expect, trust.
ἐλπίζω.as:
ἐλπίζω
[in LXX chiefly for בָּטַח, also for חָסָה, יָחַל pi., hi., etc. ;]
to look for, expect, hope (for): c. acc rei, Ro 8:24, 25, I Co 13:7, He 11:1; c. dat. rei (τ. τύχῃ, Thuc., iii, 97, 2), Mt 12:21; seq. καθώς, II Co 8:5; c. inf., Lk 6:3423:8, Ac 26:7, Ro 15:24, I Co 16:7, II Co 5:11, Phl 2:19, 23, I Ti 3:14, II Jo 12, III Jo 14; seq. ὅτι, c. pres., Lk 24:21; c. fut., Ac 24:26, II Co 1:1313:6, Phm 22. As in LXX (WM, § xxxiii, d; and esp. in the pf., Ellic. on I Ti 4:10; Bl., § 59, 2), c. prep.; εἰς, Jo 5:45 (v. Ellis., l.c.), I Pe 3:5; seq. ὅτι, II Co 1:10; ἐπί, c. dat., Ro 15:12(LXX), I Ti 4:106:17; ἐν, I Co 15:19; c. acc, I Pe 1:13 (aor. imper. v. Bl., § 58, 2); τ. θεόν, I Ti 5:5 (of. ἀπ-, προ-ελπίζω, v. Cremer, 255).†

ἐλεύθερος.sd: unrestrained (to go at pleasure), i.e. (as a citizen) not a slave (whether freeborn or manumitted), or (genitive case) exempt (from obligation or liability)
ἐλεύθερος.der: probably from the alternate of G2064 (ἔρχομαι);
ἐλεύθερος.as:
ἐλεύθερος, -α, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for חׇפְשִׁי ;]
free;
(a) in civil sense, not a slave: Jo 8:33, I Co 7:21, 2212:13, Ga 3:28, Eph 6:8, Col 3:11, Re 6:1513:1619:18; fem., Ga 4:22, 23, 30;
(b) as regards restraint and obligation in general: Mt 17:26, I Co 9:1; seq. ἐκ, I Co 9:19; ἀπό, Ro 7:3; c. inf., I Co 7:39; from the law, Ga 4:26, I Pe 2:16; from sin, Jo 8:36; τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, as regards righteousness, Ro 6:20 (Cremer, 249).†

ἐλέγχω.long: (a) I reprove, rebuke, discipline, (b) I expose, show to be guilty.
ἐλέγχω.kj: convict, convince, tell a fault, rebuke, reprove
ἐλέγχω.as:
ἐλέγχω
[in LXX chiefly for יָכַח hi. ;]
1. in Hom., to treat with contempt.
2.to convict: c. acc, Mt 18:15 (RV, show him his fault), Tit 1:9; seq. περί, Jo 8:4616:8, Ju 15; pass., Ja 2:9.
3.to reprove, rebuke: I Ti 5:20, II Ti 4:2, Tit 1:132:15, Re 3:19; pass., seq. περί, Lk 3:19; ὑπό, He 12:5(LXX).
4.to expose: Eph 5:11; pass., Jo 3:20, I Co 14:24 (RV reprove, mg. convict), Eph 5:13 (RV, as 1 Co, l.c., of. AR on Eph 5:11; MM, Exp., xii; cf. ἐξ-, δια-κατ-ελέγχομαι).†
SYN.: ἐπιτιμῶ, expressing simply rebuke, which may be un­deserved (Mt 16:22) or ineffectual (Lk 23:40), while ἐλ. implies rebuke which brings conviction (v. Tr., Syn., § iv)

ἐλαία.long: an olive tree; the Mount of Olives.
ἐλαία.sd: an olive (the tree or the fruit)
ἐλαία.der: feminine of a presumed derivative from an obsolete primary;
ἐλαία.as:
ἐλαία
(Attic, ἐλάα), -ας, ἡ[in LXX for זַיִת ;]
1.an olive tree: Ro 11:17, 24, Re 11:4; τ. ὄρος τῶν ἐ. (הַר הַוֵּתִים, Za 14:4), the Mount of Olives: Mt 21:124:326:30, Mk 11:113:314:26, Lk 19:3722:39; τὸ καλούμενον ἐ. (T, ἐλαιών, q.v.), Lk 19:2921:37.
2.an olive (Aristoph.): Ja 3:12.†

ἔλαιον.der: neuter of the same as G1636 (ἐλαία);
ἔλαιον.as:
ἔλαιον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁמֶן ;]
olive-oil: Lk 16:6, Re 6:618:13; for lamps, Mt 25:3, 4, 8; for healing, Mk 6:13, Lk 10:34, Jo 5:14; for anointing at feasts, Lk 7:46, He 1:9(LXX).†
SYN.: μύρον, ointment, v. Tr., Syn., 135

ἐλαύνω.long: (a) trans: I drive (on), propel, (b) intrans: I row.
ἐλαύνω.sd: to push (as wind, oars or dæmonical power)
ἐλαύνω.der: a prolonged form of a primary verb (obsolete except in certain tenses as an alternative of this) of uncertain affinity;
ἐλαύνω.as:
ἐλαύνω
[in LXX: Is 41:7 (הָלַם) 33:21 (שַׁיִט), etc. ;]
to drive: of the wind, Ja 3:4, II Pe 2:17; of sailors rowing or sailing a boat, Mk 6:48, Jo 6:19; of demons, Lk 8:29 (cf. ἀπ-, συν-ελαύνω).†

Ἑλληνίς.as:
Ἑλληνίς
[in LXX: II Mac 6:8 A * ;]
a Greek (i.e. Gentile) woman: Mk 7:26, Ac 17:12.†

ἐλωΐ.der: of Chaldean origin (H0426 with pronominal suffix) my God
ἐλωΐ.as:
ἐλωί
(-ΐ Rec.; ἑλωΐ LT; Aram. אֱלָהּ),
Eloi: Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34(LXX).†

Ἐλισάβετ.long: Elizabeth, mother of John the Baptizer.

Ἐλμαδάμ.long: Elmadam, father of Cosam, son of Er.
Ἐλμαδάμ.as:
Ἐλμαδάμ (L, Ἑλ-; Rec. -μωδάμ), ό, indecl.,
Elmadam, an ancestor of Jesus: Lk 3:28.

Ἐλιέζερ.long: Eliezer, son of Joram and father of Joshua.
Ἐλιέζερ.as:
Ἐλιέζερ(Heb. אֱלִיעֶזֶר), ὁ, indecl.,
Eliezer, an ancestor of Jesus: Lk 3:29.†

Ἐλισαῖος.as:
Ἐλισαῖος (Rec. Ἐλισσαῖος; T, Ἑλισ-), -ου, ὁ (Heb. אֱלִישָׁע),
Elisha, the prophet: Lk 4:27.†

ἑλκόομαι.long: I afflict with sores; pass: I am afflicted with sores.
ἑλκόομαι.sd: to cause to ulcerate, i.e. (passively) be ulcerous
ἑλκόομαι.as:
* ἑλκόω, -ῶ
1.to wound.
2.to ulcerate; pass., to suffer from sores: pf. ptcp., εἱλκωμίνος (Rec. ἡλκ-), EV, full of sores, Lk 16:20.†

ἕλκος.as:
ἕλκος, -εος (-ους), τό
[in LXX: Ex 9:9-11, Le 13:18-27, IV Ki 20:7, Jb 2:7 (שְׁחִין) ;]
1.a wound (Hom.).
2.a sore, an ulcer (Thuc., al.): Lk 16:21, Re 16:2, 11.†

ἐλάσσων.sd: smaller (in size, quantity, age or quality)
ἐλάσσων.der: comparative of the same as G1646 (ἐλάχιστος);
ἐλάσσων.as:
ἐλάσσων (-ττων, He 7:7, WH, 1 Ti 5:9), -ον
(formed, with superl. ἐλάχιστος, from the epic ἐλαχύς, little, and serving as compar. of μικρός), [in LXX for מָעַט, etc. ;]
less, in age, rank or quality: Jo 2:19, Ro 9:12(LXX), He 7:7; neut., -ον, adverbially: I Ti 5:9.†

ἐλαττόω.as:
ἐλαττόω, -ῶ
(< ἐλάιττων), [in LXX (where also -σσῶ) chiefly for חָסֵר, and very freq. in Si;]
to make less: He 2:7(LXX); pass., Jo 3:30, He 2:9.†

ἕλκω.long: I drag, draw, pull, persuade, unsheathe.
ἕλκω.as:
ἕλκω
(Hellenistic form ἑλκύω in Jo, ll. c., Ac 16:19), [in LXX for מָשַׁךְ, etc. ;]
to draw: c. acc rei, Jo 18:1021:6; c. acc pers., seq. ἔξω, Ac 21:30; εἰς, Ac 16:19, Ja 2:6. Metaph., to draw, lead, impel: Jo 6:4412:32. (For discussion of ἕ. in Oxyrh. Log., v. Deiss., LAE, 437 ff.)†

Ἕλλην.long: a Hellene, the native word for a Greek; it is, however, a term wide enough to include all Greek-speaking (i.e. educated) non-Jews.
Ἕλλην.sd: a Hellen (Grecian) or inhabitant of Hellas; by extension a Greek-speaking person, especially a non-Jew
Ἕλλην.as:
Ἕλλην, -ηνος, ὁ
[in LXX: Jl 3:6, Za 9:13 (יָוָן), etc.; I Mac 1:10, al. * ;]
a Greek; opp. to βάρβαρος, Ro 1:14; usually in ΝΤ of Greek Gentiles, opp. to Ἰουδαῖοι: Jo 7:35, Ac 11:2014:116:1, 318:419:10, 1720:2121:28, Ro 1:162:9, 103:910:12, I Co 1:22, 2410:3212:13, Ga 2:33:28, Col 3:11; of proselytes, Jo 12:20, Ac 17:4.†

ἐλευθερόω.sd: to liberate, i.e. (figuratively) to exempt (from moral, ceremonial or mortal liability)
ἐλευθερόω.as:
ἐλευθερόω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Pr 25:10. II Mac 1:272:22 * ;]
to make free: from sin, Jo 8:32, 36; seq. ἀπό, Ro 6:18, 228:2, 21; τ. ἐλευθερία (dat. commodi), Ga 5:1 (on the "punctiliar" force of this verb, v. M, Pr. 149; cf. also Cremer, 251).†

Ἑλληνιστί.sd: Hellenistically, i.e. in the Grecian language
Ἑλληνιστί.der: adverb from the same as G1675 (Ἑλληνιστής);
Ἑλληνιστί.as:
* Ἑλληνιστί
adv.,
in Greek: Jo 19:20; Ἑ. (sc. λαλεῖν) γινώσκεις, Ac 21:37 (cf. Field, Notes, 135).†

ἐλαιών.sd: an olive-orchard, i.e. (specially) the Mount of Olives
ἐλαιών.as:
† ἐλαιών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(< ἐλαία), [in LXX for זַיִת ;]
olive-grove, olive-garden (so in FlJ and in π.; Deiss., BS, 209 ff.; MM, Exp., iii; M, Pr., 49, 69, 235): Lk 19:2921:37 (WH, -ῶν; v. their App., 158; Field, Notes, 73; Bl., § 10, 5; 33, 1; Thayer, s.v.), Ac 1:12 (where Bl, ll. c., proposes the conjectural emendation ἐλαιῶν for -ῶνος).†

Ἐλαμίτης.long: an Elamite, one of a people living to the north of the Persian Gulf in the southern part of Persia.
Ἐλαμίτης.as:
Ἐλαμείτης (Rec. -αμίτης), -ου, ὁ
(Heb. אֵילָם) [in LXX (cl.) Ἐλυμαίος, Ἔλαμος: Jth 1:6; Ἀιλαμείτης (vv.ll. Ἐλ-, -αμίτης; Bl., § 3, 7): Is 11:1121:222:6) ;]
an Elamite: Ac 2:9.†

ἐλπίς.der: from a primary (to anticipate, usually with pleasure);
ἐλπίς.as:
ἐλπίς
(ἑλ-, Ro 8:20, WH, v. Bl., § 4, 3; M, Pr., 44), -ίδος, ἡ[in LXX for בָּטַח and its derivatives, תִּקְוָה (freq. in Jb), etc. ;]
expectation (in cl., rarely of evil, mostly of good, and so always in NT), hope;
1. of hope in general: II Co 1:6; c. gen. obj., Ac 16:19; art. inf., Ac 27:20, I Co 9:10; παρ’ ἐλπίδα, Ro 4:18; ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι, I Co 9:10.
2. Of religious hope: ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι, Ac 2:2626:6, Ro 4:188:20, Tit 1:2; τῇ ἐ. ἐσώθημεν, Ro 8:24; κατ' ἐλπίδα ζωῆς αἰωνίου, Tit 3:7; of the Messianic hope of Israel, Ac 23:626:6, 728:20; of Christian hope, Ro 5:2, 4, 512:1215:4, 13, I Co 13:13, II Th 2:16, He 3:66:117:1910:23, I Pe 1:3, 213:15; c. gen. obj., Ro 5:2, Col 1:27, I Th 1:35:8, Tit 1:2; c. gen. of that on which the hope is based, Ac 26:6, Eph 1:184:4, Col 1:23; ὁ θεὸς τῆς ἐ., Ro 15:13; ἔχειν ἐ. (= cl. ἐλπίζειν), Ac 24:15, Ro 15:4, II Co 3:1210:15, Eph 2:12, I Th 4:13; seq. ἐπί, c. dat., I Jo 3:3; εἰς, Ac 24:15; ὅτι, Ro 8:20, Phl 1:20, 21. Meton.,
(a) of the author or ground of hope (cl.): I Th 2:19, I Ti 1:1; c. gen. obj., Col 1:27;
(b) of the thing hoped for: Ga 5:5, Col 1:5, Tit 2:13, He 6:18 (Cremer, 252, 712).†

Ἑλληνιστής.long: a Hellenist, Grecian Jew, a Greek-speaking Jew, that is one who can speak Greek only and not Hebrew (or Aramaic).
Ἑλληνιστής.as:
*† Ἑλληνιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< Ἑλληνίζω, to Hellenize, affect Greek cus­toms),
a Hellenist (RV, Grecian Jew): Ac 6:19:2911:20.†

Ἐλύμας.long: Elymas, the name of the sorcerer at Paphos.
Ἐλύμας.as:
Ἐλύμας, -α, ὁ
(< Aram. or Arab., cf. DB, i, 246 b)
Elymas: Ac 13:8.†

Ἑλλάς.long: Hellas, the native name for Greece.
Ἑλλάς.sd: Hellas (or Greece), a country of Europe
Ἑλλάς.as:
Ἑλλάς, -άδος, ἡ
[in LXX: Is 66:19, Ez 27:13 (יָוָן), I Mac 1:1 8:9 * ;]
with varying usage as to geographical limits; in NT = 'Αχαία (cf. Ac 18:12),
Greece: Ac 20:2.†

ἐλλογέω.g: I charge to, put to one's account
ἐλλογέω.long: I charge to, put to one's account, impute.
ἐλλογέω.der: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3056 (λόγος) (in the sense of account);
ἐλλογέω.as:
*† ἐλλογάω, -ῶ
(a κοινή word, elsewhere usually -έω; cf. Bl., § 22, 2),
to charge to one's account, impute: Phm 18 (on parallels, cf. Deiss., LAE, 79 f., 335 f.; Milligan, NTD, 73; MM, Exp., xii); of sin, Ro 5:13 (Cremer, 400).†

ἐλευθερία.long: freedom, liberty, especially: a state of freedom from slavery.
ἐλευθερία.sd: freedom (legitimate or licentious, chiefly moral or ceremonial)
ἐλευθερία.as:
ἐλευθερία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Le 19:20 (חֻפְשָׁה), I Es 4:49, 53, Si 7:21, 33:25, I Mac 14:27, III Mac 3:28 * ;]
liberty: with reference to the religious life, I Co 10:29, II Co 3:17, Ga 2:45:1, I Pe 2:16, II Pe 2:19; ὁ νόμος τῆς ἐ., Ja 1:252:12; ἡ ἐ. τῆς δόξης, Ro 8:21; ἐπ’ ἐ., Ga 5:13 (on which formula, cf. Deiss., LAE, 327 ff.; Cremer, 251).†

ἐλεεινός.as:
ἐλεεινός, -ή, -όν
(< ἔλεος in Re, l.c., WH have the Attic poëtic form, ἐλεινός),
pitiable, miserable: Re 3:17; comparat., I Co 15:19.†

ἐλαττονέω.as:
† ἐλαττονέω, -ῶ
(< ἔλαττον), [in LXX (with -όω) chiefly for חָסֵר ;]
to be less (RV, had no lack): II Co 8:15(LXX) (a rare word; cf. MM, Exp., xii).†

ἐλεγμός.long: a proof, possibly: a persuasion; reproof.
ἐλεγμός.as:
† ἐλεγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ἐλέγχω), [in LXX: Ps 38:1439:11 (תּוֹכֵחָה), Si 20:2921:641:4, al. ;]
reproof: II Ti 3:16.†

ἑλίσσω.long: I roll, roll up, fold up.
ἑλίσσω.as:
ἑλίσσω
[in LXX: Is 34:4 (גָּלַל ni.), Ps 102:26 (חָלַף hi.), etc. ;]
to roll, roll up: He 1:12(LXX), Re 6:14.†

ἔλεγχος.long: a proof, possibly: a persuasion; reproof.
ἔλεγχος.as:
ἔλεγχος, -ου, ὁ
(ἐλέγχω) [in LXX: freq. in Pr, Jb (תּוֺכַחַת) Wi 5, Si 3, etc. ;]
a proof, test: He 11:1.†

ἔλεγξις.as:
† ἔλεγξις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἐλέγχω), [in LXX: Jb 21:423:2 (שִׂיחַ) * ;]
rebuke: II Pe 2:16.†

Ἑλληνικός.as:
Ἑλληνικκός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX: Je 46:650:16 (יָנָה: aliter in Heb.), II Mac 4:10, 156:911:2413:2, IV Mac 8:8 * ;]
Greek: τ. Ἑλληνικῇ (sc. γλωσσῇ), Re 9:11.†

ἐλεφάντινος.sd: elephantine, i.e. (by implication) composed of ivory
ἐλεφάντινος.as:
ἐλεφάντινος, -η, -ον
(< ἐλέφας, ivory), [in LXX for שֵׁן ;]
of ivory: Re 18:12.†
